note: Seed product directory. Pick a product and its company and sub-processors come with it. Everything here must be verified against the supplier's current terms before a card is marked 'on file'; treat these as starting points, not facts. Fields marked [verify] are placeholders. 'plans' says what each plan of a product allows: the same product is a different thing on its free, business and enterprise plans, and the plan decides the tier it may take (it overrides the sanctioned list). Research notes are from November 2026 and are secondary sources unless marked.

microsoft.name: Microsoft
microsoft.notes: Products and Services DPA covers M365, Copilot (enterprise), Power Platform, Azure. Consumer Copilot is a different product. The Anthropic models offered inside Copilot sit outside the EU Data Boundary (Microsoft docs); switch them off in the admin centre for Tier 2 flows.

openai_azure.name: OpenAI via Azure
openai_azure.notes: Sub-processor to Microsoft for Copilot and Azure OpenAI. Covered by the Microsoft DPA.

google.name: Google
google.notes: Workspace for Education has its own terms; consumer Gemini is different.

canva.name: Canva
canva.notes: Education terms exist. Check training on inputs for AI features.

lovable.name: Lovable
lovable.notes: Hosting and AI gateway. DPA on Business and Enterprise. Free and Pro users are opted in to model training by default (Account Settings, Privacy). Hosting region is selectable but the terms don't guarantee a region for AI gateway requests below Enterprise. AI subprocessor list is 'available on request', so get it in writing.

replit.name: Replit
replit.notes: Hosted on Google Cloud in the US, no European hosting. DPA on Pro and Enterprise only. Sources disagree on whether private code is used for training; ask in writing.

base44.name: Base44 (Wix)
base44.notes: Data controlled by Wix in Israel; Wix is on the UK extension of the Data Privacy Framework. The privacy policy says prompts and usage data are used to improve services including machine learning models; third-party reports say only Enterprise is excluded. DPA for app-visitor data.

supabase.name: Supabase
supabase.notes: Runs on AWS; region selectable at project creation (e.g. eu-west-2 London).

openai_consumer.name: OpenAI (ChatGPT)
openai_consumer.notes: Free and Plus train on chats unless opted out and have no DPA. Business (was Team) and Enterprise: DPA, no training, 30-day default retention. UK data residency is Enterprise only.

anthropic_consumer.name: Anthropic (Claude)
anthropic_consumer.notes: Claude.ai personal accounts are consumer terms. Team, Enterprise and API: DPA included, no training by default. Zero retention and EU residency are Enterprise only.

xai.name: xAI (Grok)
xai.notes: xAI says business inputs are not used for training, but sources disagree on whether the DPA meets Article 28, processing is described as global including the USA, and the ICO opened an inquiry into xAI in 2025. Not approved for personal data on any plan until that settles.

power_platform.name: Power Automate / Power Apps / Power BI

custom_app.name: An app we're building
custom_app.notes: Building is cheap now; running is what matters. The hosting choice below decides who holds the data, under which contract, and which tier it may take.

custom_app_m365.name: An app we build, run in our Microsoft tenant
custom_app_m365.notes: Power Apps, or a React app on Azure with Microsoft sign-in and the Graph API. Inside the Microsoft contract you already have, so Tier 2 is allowed, as long as no outside AI provider is wired in.

supplier_questions: Are we using this under an organisational agreement or personal accounts?
Is there a data processing agreement, and does it cover this specific service?
Where is our data stored and processed (country and region)?
What happens to uploads, prompts, outputs and logs, and for how long are they kept?
Can you confirm our data is not used to train models?
Which other companies process our data on your behalf (sub-processors), and how will we be told of changes?
How do we delete our data, and how do you confirm deletion?
How do you help us answer a subject access request or a breach?
Can you provide evidence of your security measures (certification or audit)?
Have you published a DPIA or a data protection summary for this product?
